title: Matt Helders - Wikipedia
notes: Matthew Helders, born 7 May 1986, Sheffield. Took up the drums because the others already had guitars: drums 'was the only thing left'. Rap: 'We were rap fans at school more than now ... it still influences us in some ways; like for me, it's the drummin'' (Q, 2007). Queens of the Stone Age live at a festival the biggest influence on his development: it made him want to 'start hitting harder'. The band's most prominent backing vocalist; lead on 'D Is for Dangerous', 'Brick by Brick'. Iggy Pop's Post Pop Depression (2016) and its tour; Lady Gaga's Joanne (2016); the Last Shadow Puppets (2016); Toddla T; Mongrel (Better Than Heavy, 2009); Late Night Tales (2008); produced Good Cop Bad Cop (2019); Terrific, with Tyler Parkford (2025). '0114' (Sheffield's dialling code) on the front of his kit. Plays in joggers rather than jeans.

title: Dusty Henry, 'Arctic Monkeys Drummer Matt Helders on Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino and Drumming with Restraint', KEXP, 23 October 2018
notes: 'My favorite drummers are, like, John Bonham, but also Buddy Rich, even though I don't necessarily play like either of them.' 'I liked that it was a rock drummer playing jazzier beats rather than just a jazz drummer playing these songs.' 'I think restraint is a difficult thing for drummers that I've felt in the past.' 'I think it's good when you leave something out.' 'In the past, we've sometimes written songs around the drum beat, and that's come first.' 'This time it was about playing something tasteful and a good groove for the songs.' 'It could be something like a little ghost note or a roll on the drums, and it's just attention to detail.'

title: 'Matt Helders' 7 favourite drummers of all time', Far Out Magazine
notes: A secondary write-up, citing a 2013 MusicRadar interview on his favourite drumming records (not read). John Bonham 'my favourite drummer of all time' (a fill in Moby Dick's solo: 'It gives me chills'); Questlove ('has always been a favourite of mine'); Mitch Mitchell; Dave Grohl on Songs for the Deaf ('It's hard to beat Dave Grohl, isn't it?'); the Hives' Chris Dangerous ('why my drum kit is set up the way it is', 'I wanted my drums to look like his'); Carmine Appice; Bill Ward. No quotes given for Mitchell, Appice or Ward.

title: Tom Taylor, 'Matt Helders on the drummer who inspired his new style', Far Out Magazine, 7 November 2022
notes: Questlove, on Jay-Z's MTV Unplugged (2001): 'Questlove has always been a favourite of mine.' 'Not everybody can play a simple groove for three minutes with no variation and have it mean something.' 'It sounds easy, but it's not.' 'I'd rather listen to a drummer who knows how to play to the song.' The original interview is not named.

title: 'Arctic Monkeys Drummer Matt Helders: Agile Beast', Drumhead Authority
notes: Quotes gathered from other interviews, undated. From Loud and Quiet: 'If I wanted to be in the band it was drums only. So I used to keep them in Alex's garage, and we practiced there.' 'It was a slow start. I just didn't want to be left out.' From MusicRadar: 'The first good kit I had was a Premier kit for my 18th birthday, and obviously Keith Moon played Premier.' Premier 'were a British company ... being made in England I thought that was quite important'. 'My latest Premier kit is the Union Jack one I used at the Olympics and I've been touring that.' 'I always used the same configuration, 22", 13", 16", but I went 24", 14" and 18".' 'It's the first bigger kit that I've got.' The Guardian on Favourite Worst Nightmare: 'if you removed everything from the album except Matt Helders' drumming, it would still be a pretty gripping listen.'

title: Drumeo, 'Gear Breakdown: The Iconic Drumming Behind R U Mine', 14 May 2025
notes: The kit in the R U Mine? video: Ludwig Classic Oak in Black Satin, 12x8 tom, 16x16 floor tom, 22x16 bass drum; a Ludwig Raw CopperPhonic 14x6.5 snare; Zildjian K Custom Session 14-inch hats, 18- and 19-inch K Sweet crashes, a 22-inch K Light ride; DW 6000 flat-based hardware; Remo heads. 'Blends indie rock urgency with hip-hop swagger.'

title: 'Arctic Monkeys play London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony', NME
notes: Read in a search summary only: at the ceremony's climax (27 July 2012) the band played I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor and the Beatles' Come Together; Helders in a Union Jack tracksuit, on drums emblazoned with the flag.

title: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 140,632. Released 23 January 2006 (UK), Domino; recorded June to September 2005 at the Chapel (South Thoresby), 2 Fly (Sheffield) and Telstar (Munich); produced by Jim Abbiss and Alan Smyth. Alex Turner, Jamie Cook, Andy Nicholson, Matt Helders. I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor released 17 October 2005, a UK number one. Nothing on the drums.

title: Favourite Worst Nightmare - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 104,209. Released 23 April 2007 (UK), Domino; recorded December 2006 at Miloco Garden, Eastcote, Motor Museum and Konk; produced by James Ford and Mike Crossey. Nick O'Malley's first album on bass. Singles: Brianstorm (2 April 2007), Fluorescent Adolescent (9 July 2007), Teddy Picker (3 December 2007). Helders's and O'Malley's rhythms compared to ESG; the band went dancing after James Ford's DJ sets. The Guardian: 'if you removed everything from the album except Matt Helders' drumming, it would still be a pretty gripping listen.'

title: Humbug (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 24 August 2009 (UK), Domino; recorded November 2008 to April 2009 at Pink Duck (Burbank), Rancho De La Luna (Joshua Tree) and Mission Sound (New York); Josh Homme produced tracks 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8 to 10, James Ford tracks 1, 4, 7 and 11. Crying Lightning, the first single, 6 July 2009. Clash heard 'circus-like marching drums'.

title: AM (Arctic Monkeys album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 212,662. Released 6 September 2013, Domino; recorded January 2012 to June 2013 at Sage & Sound and Vox (Los Angeles) and Rancho De La Luna; produced by James Ford, co-produced by Ross Orton. Helders on drums, backing vocals and handclaps. Recorded with the bass and drums laid down first, for the groove; his kit often set up in unusual ways for different sounds. The band's first hip-hop-influenced sound: Turner wanted a 'Dr. Dre beat' feel. Singles: R U Mine? (27 February 2012), Do I Wanna Know? (19 June 2013), Arabella (UK, 10 March 2014).

title: Arctic Monkeys, 'I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor', Glastonbury, Pyramid Stage, 28 June 2013 (BBC), YouTube c-wwK5QVv1Y
notes: Frames read at 0:37 to 0:43 and 2:27 to 2:59: short dark-brown hair, short at the back and sides, swept up and back on top; clean-shaven; a black sleeveless top with a small white print on the chest; dark trousers laced up the outside of the leg; in-ear monitors, no headphones. A shell kit in a dark grey-black pearl under the lights, chrome hardware, one rack tom, a floor tom, crashes high on his left and right; the stage lit cyan and white.
